newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma doubles jail sentence of Suu Kyi's aide.
newsitem.headline: Burma doubles jail sentence of Suu Kyi's aide.

text.p: Burma's military government added seven extra years to double the jail term for Win Htein, the personal assistant for democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, a dissident source said on Wednesday.
"They added seven years, so he now must serve altogether 14 years," an official from Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party told Reuters.
He said the additional term was given on August 30, but he did not know the reason.
"We don't know why they added to his term," he said.
Last month the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) sentenced Win Htein to seven years at Insein Prison under section five of the Emergency Provisions Act.
The government announced the sentence last week and said Win Htein was being held for "malicious acts aimed at destruction of the peace and stability of the state."
It said he took part in a "conspiracy" to make a video fabricating the poor situation of Burmese farmers.
Suu Kyi said in a news conference on Saturday that Win Htein had not taken part in making the video but had only set up a time for her to meet the party members who had made the video.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.
Win Htein was one of the 262 NLD members detained in May in a sweeping crackdown on the democracy movement ahead of a controversial party meeting.
The SLORC, which said it had made the detentions in an effort to avoid anarchy from the meeting, released most of the activists but kept several dozen in detention.
Most of those still detained were key members of Suu Kyi's party, diplomats said. Many have been given long jail sentences.
